title: Three-Year Squad Planning: Can Mumbai Indians Build Beyond One Season?
dek: Can Mumbai Indians build beyond one season? Squad continuity, the share of each season's work done by returning players, shows how much they plan in cycles.
excerpt: On average, Mumbai Indians' returning players have done a measurable share of each season's batting and bowling. Mega-auctions reset that number; good planning keeps a core through them.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Seasons or Cycles
body: IPL squads are rebuilt at mega-auctions every few years and adjusted at mini-auctions in between. A franchise that plans in three-year cycles keeps a core through the reset; one that plans season by season rebuilds from scratch.
On average {{ev:cont-avg}} of Mumbai Indians' runs scored and balls bowled have come from players who also played for them the season before.

sections.heading: Where the Resets Came
body: Their most continuous season was {{ev:cont-hi}} and their least continuous {{ev:cont-lo}}. In 2026, returning players did {{ev:cont-last}} of the work.
In seasons that followed a mega-auction, returning players did {{ev:cont-mega}} of the work on average, against {{ev:cont-other}} in other seasons.

sections.heading: Planning Through the Reset
body: A three-year plan names the core roles to keep, the ones to buy and the young players to develop into the next core. Retention choices then follow from the plan rather than from the last season's form.
For MI, that means deciding at each mini-auction which players are meant to be in the next mega-auction's retention list.

sections.heading: Continuity Is Not Always Good
body: Keeping a core is only valuable if the core is good. A franchise can be highly continuous and consistently mediocre.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Plan the Core Three Years Out
body: Mumbai Indians should plan their core across auction cycles and treat each mini-auction as a step towards the next mega-auction.
Continuity should be a result of that plan, not a goal in itself.
